ledger.claim: The driver's own telemetry shows there is no route deviation on this trip at all: the measured excess over the 11.2 km optimal route is -0.2 km, or -1.8%, so neither limb of POL-RD-01 is met — the excess is nowhere near the 20% and the 0.8 km that must BOTH be exceeded before a deviation is ESTABLISHED. With no deviation there is no detour, no excess distance and no ground on which any sum can be moved on a deviation theory.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip (quoted_fare_sgd 23.00 against charged_total 26.00), so POL-RD-11 governs and the POL-RD-02 distance-and-time recomputation does not run: the rider can claim no distance refund and can be billed nothing beyond the quote plus the pass-through lines. On the ledger's own figures there is no contested sum to move — charged 26.00 less quoted 23.00 less the single SGD 3.00 ERP line leaves exactly the SGD 0.00 the ledger publishes as pol_rd_11_remedy — so nothing is owing from this fare to either party.

The driver's prayer — 'release that SGD 3 to me' — is not a remedy any clause of the policy creates. POL-RD-09 characterises an ERP charge as a third-party, government-set pass-through settled separately from distance and time charges and never counted twice; the clauses that can move money to a driver are POL-RD-04, which requires the rider to have been billed for less distance than the trace records and which fails here because the ledger bills 11.0 km against an 11.0 km trace with no shortfall, and POL-RD-12, which applies only where the vehicle is RYDE_POOL and this vehicle is RYDE_X. Nothing in the loaded policy entitles the driver to have a pass-through line paid out to him as a contested sum.

The fare already carries the ERP line and the payment is still PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the present state is that nothing has been collected from the rider and nothing has been released to the driver. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION on this driver-filed dispute leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd exactly as they stand, and it never means the charge is restored or processed; on this record the only outcome the evidence supports is to leave the payment state untouched and refuse the driver's claimed entitlement.

The rider's destination change supplies the driver with no additional entitlement either. POL-RD-05 re-bases the POL-RD-01 test on the amended endpoints and the amended optimal is 11.2 km / 20.0 minutes, numerically identical to the booked optimal, so the recomputation yields no surviving deviation and POL-RD-05 expressly provides that the outcome is then NO_ACTION; and the amendment is timestamped 16:27:40, more than three minutes AFTER the gantry was charged at 16:24:40, so on the ledger's own timestamps the change neither created nor removed the line. POL-RD-05 adjusts a distance baseline; it creates no charge and no payment.

So far as the driver relies on the SGD 3.00 line being 'properly chargeable' under POL-RD-09 and POL-RD-11(a), the record does not establish that against the baseline the policy mandates. POL-RD-05 makes the AMENDED endpoints the governing baseline for this trip, yet the bundle publishes no amended-route ERP analysis and no amended-route ERP total: the on_optimal_route flag on the line does not state which optimal route it was assessed against, and the amended-route figure (amended_optimal_distance_km 11.2) is a distance only. Whether the Canal Corridor gantry lies on the amended optimal route is therefore unverified anywhere in the bundle, and an unverified pass-through should not be released to the driver on this record.

The bundle holds no traffic advisory for this trip: EV-ADVIS-00709-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window. That absence is itself citable, and it means no external traffic cause can be asserted for anything that occurred on this trip — POL-RD-03 is unavailable for want of any advisory record and any such assertion would carry no weight under POL-RD-13. Nothing in the exculpatory record reallocates or excuses the disputed SGD 3.

The GPS trace governs distance under POL-RD-01, and it records trace_distance_km of 11.0 km against an optimal of 11.2 km - an excess of -0.2 km (-1.79%), as the derived deviation block confirms. Both establishment tests fail (excess must exceed 0.8 km in absolute terms AND 20% of optimal): there is no deviation on this trip at all, so no distance charge is refundable and the fare bills exactly the distance driven.

The destination was amended at 16:27:40 (trip_record.dropoff_amended_at, matched to the rider's 16:27:40 chat message), so POL-RD-05 requires POL-RD-01 to be re-applied against the amended endpoints: amended_optimal_distance_km 11.2 km with amended_optimal_duration_min 20.0 min. Driving 11.0 km against an amended optimal of 11.2 km again yields no excess, and POL-RD-05 directs NO_ACTION where no deviation survives the recomputation. Distance driven before the amendment timestamp is never counted as excess against the driver.

The SGD 3.00 'Canal Corridor entry' line is properly chargeable, not refundable. The fare_breakdown records it on_optimal_route true, and the trace passes it at a nearest-fix distance of 0.0 m (fix index 36 at 16:24:40), well inside POL-RD-09's 250 m match radius. POL-RD-09(4)'s billing-integrity refund reaches only a gantry the trace never passes; this gantry is matched, so the pass-through line stands and the SGD 3 is not a phantom or off-route charge.

The destination change was rider-caused, and it came after the gantry crossing. The rider's own message at 16:27:40 reads 'I changed the destination in the app', and the driver replied at 16:27:50 'We passed the ERP entry before you changed it'; the gantry was charged at 16:24:40, three minutes earlier. Under POL-RD-09(3) a rider-caused relocation under POL-RD-05 attracts no ERP refund to the rider.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip (quoted_fare_sgd 23.00, charged_total 26.00). POL-RD-11 limits the rider's money remedy to the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quoted fare plus properly chargeable pass-throughs: 26.00 - 23.00 - 3.00 = 0.00, exactly the published pol_rd_11_remedy of 0.00, and to a POL-RD-09 correction for off-route or phantom lines, of which there are none. No sum is refundable to the rider, and the SGD 3.00 ERP stands as a correctly billed pass-through.

The bundle holds no advisory covering this corridor - EV-ADVIS-00709-01 is MISSING, carries issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, so it can carry no fact. That absence does not weaken the driver here, because no party asserts an external traffic cause: the only cause on the record is the rider's own amendment, which the chat log records. POL-RD-03 cannot be run against an advisory that does not exist, but nothing in this case turns on it.

ruling.explanation:
To the driver and to the rider: this dispute is decided on the fare record and the GPS trace, and it leaves both of you where you already are.

The driver's request — that the SGD 3.00 ERP line be released to him — cannot be granted. The SGD 3.00 is the 'Canal Corridor entry' charge. The fare breakdown records it as on the optimal route, and the GPS trace passes the gantry at a nearest-fix distance of 0.0 m at 16:24:40, so it is a real crossing of a real on-route gantry, properly chargeable as a government pass-through under POL-RD-09. No clause turns an ERP pass-through into a payment to the driver: POL-RD-04 driver compensation requires the rider to have been billed for more than 1.0 km less than the trace records, and here the ledger bills 11.0 km against an 11.0 km trace — no shortfall — while POL-RD-12 applies only to RYDE_POOL trips and this was a RYDE_X trip. POL-RD-11(a) fixes an UPFRONT_QUOTE rider's remedy at charged_total 26.00 less quoted_fare 23.00 less the properly chargeable pass-through of 3.00, which is exactly the 0.00 the ledger publishes as pol_rd_11_remedy: nothing is owing from this fare to either party.

There is likewise no deviation to refund to the rider or to charge to the driver. The governing trace figure is 11.0 km under POL-RD-01, against an optimal of 11.2 km — an excess of -0.2 km, or -1.8%. Both establishment tests fail (the excess must exceed 0.8 km and 20% of optimal), and re-running the test on the amended endpoints under POL-RD-05 gives the same amended optimal of 11.2 km / 20.0 min and the same negative excess, so POL-RD-05's own direction is NO_ACTION. The destination amendment is timestamped 16:27:40, after the gantry was charged at 16:24:40, so it neither created nor removed the ERP line.

The rider's point that the amended baseline leaves the gantry unverified is rejected: the trace crossed the gantry on the route as actually driven at 16:24:40, before the amendment, and the line is flagged on the optimal route. There is no traffic advisory on file (EV-ADVIS-00709-01 is missing, weight 0.0), and because no party asserts an external traffic cause, POL-RD-03 has no advisory to run against and plays no part.

The outcome is NO_ACTION: the fare stands, payment_status remains PENDING and refund_issued_sgd remains 0.00, left exactly as they are. No money moves to either party, and no referral is produced — there is no material deviation and no repeat-pattern finding for a POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral, and no phantom or off-route line for a POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
